names_page.tithi_note: The page gives a 15-day pattern plus 30 Amavasya, with no Paksha headings. The daily pages print Krishna days 1 to 14 with the same names (for example '(Asvina Krishna) Tritiya').
names_page.karana_note: One unnumbered line. The page alone does not say which Karana is repeating or fixed or where each falls.

explanation_quotes.tithi: Tithi is the time period during which the moon gains 12 degrees or its integral multiples in longitude on the sun.
explanation_quotes.ending_moments: The timings given against tithi, nakshatra, yoga and karana are their ending moments (i.e., when the span of the phenomena is completed).
explanation_quotes.karana: Karana is the time period during which the moon gains 6 degrees in longitude on the sun, and thus there are two karanas covering two half periods of tithimana.
explanation_quotes.karana_repeating: There are 7 karanas which repeat in a cyclic order starting from 2nd half of sukla pratipada and ending at 1st half of Krishna chaturdasi.
explanation_quotes.karana_fixed: There are 4 sthira or non-recurring karanas which cover the period from 2nd half of Krishna chaturdasi to 1st half of sukla pratipada.
explanation_quotes.yoga: Yoga is calculated from the sum of the nirayana longitudes of the sun and moon.
explanation_quotes.yoga_first: When this sum amounts to 13° 20' the first yoga ends, when it amounts to 26° 40’ the second yoga ends and so on.
explanation_quotes.yoga_count: There are in all 27 yogas covering 360°.

daily_kartika_1948.note: One row per civil date, in printed order. Tithi entries are [paksha as printed, name as printed, ending time]; Karana and Yoga entries are [name as printed, ending time]. 'ahoratra' means no ending in that sunrise-to-sunrise day. Nakshatra and astronomy fields are not recorded.
